appeals.name: UN Global Humanitarian Appeal 2026
appeals.latest: The UN and aid partners launched a $33 billion appeal to support 135 million people through 23 country operations and six refugee or migrant plans.
appeals.brief: The 2026 appeal is the top-level humanitarian financing benchmark. The analytical priority is funding conversion into country plans, because the launch figure is a requirement—not cash received.
appeals.fundingNote: Funding receipts must be reconciled against the live OCHA Financial Tracking Service.
appeals.delivery: UN-coordinated country and regional response plans
appeals.coordinator: UN OCHA with UN agencies and humanitarian partners
milestones: Funding and delivery tracked through OCHA FTS and country plans

appeals.name: UNICEF Humanitarian Action for Children 2026
appeals.geography: 35 country, multi-country, regional and global appeals
appeals.latest: UNICEF opened 35 humanitarian appeals requiring $7.66 billion to assist more than 73 million vulnerable children, families and caregivers.
appeals.brief: This is a portfolio of child-centred emergency programmes rather than one undifferentiated fund. Monitor funding by country appeal and by service line: health, nutrition, WASH, education and child protection.
appeals.fundingNote: Current receipts are published in country situation reports and should not be inferred from the appeal requirement.
appeals.delivery: UNICEF country offices with government and implementing partners
milestones: Country situation reports update funding and delivery

appeals.name: FAO Global Emergency & Resilience Appeal 2026
appeals.latest: FAO launched its first global Emergency and Resilience Appeal, seeking $2.5 billion to assist more than 100 million people in 54 countries.
appeals.brief: The programme is designed around restoring local production, not only emergency consumption. FAO reports that each dollar invested in a farmer’s field produces about $3 in local food value, while just 5% of relevant funding supports food production.
appeals.fundingNote: The appeal supports earmarked, soft-earmarked and flexible SFERA contributions.
appeals.delivery: FAO country operations with ministries, local organizations and NGOs
milestones: Emergency and resilience support reached 42.4 million people

appeals.name: WHO Health Emergency Appeal 2025
appeals.latest: WHO requested $1.5 billion for 42 health emergencies, including 17 Grade 3 emergencies requiring its highest level of response.
appeals.brief: The appeal protects emergency health services, outbreak control and continuity of care. Compare the published requirement with country-level allocations before drawing conclusions about geographic coverage.
appeals.fundingNote: The public appeal summary states the requirement but not a consolidated current receipt total.
appeals.delivery: WHO country offices and health-cluster partners
milestones: Country and flash appeals updated as emergencies evolved

appeals.name: IDA21 Concessional Financing Package
appeals.latest: IDA21 entered implementation with up to $100 billion in grants and low-interest finance, backed by up to $23.7 billion in donor contributions from more than 60 donors.
appeals.brief: IDA21 is concessional development finance, not a humanitarian appeal; donor contributions are leveraged into a larger financing package. Track commitments and disbursements separately, and do not label the $100 billion package as grant aid.
appeals.fundingNote: $23.7 billion is the donor-contribution component; the $100 billion package includes leveraged financing. A funding-coverage percentage would be invalid.
appeals.delivery: Grants and zero- to low-interest credits through IDA country programmes

appeals.name: UNHCR Global Appeal 2025
appeals.latest: UNHCR presented a $10.248 billion appeal to protect and assist a projected 139.3 million forcibly displaced and stateless people across 136 countries and territories.
appeals.brief: The appeal combines protection, basic needs, emergency response and durable solutions. The operative comparison is between outcome-area budgets and subsequent funding—not a single undifferentiated “refugee aid” number.
appeals.fundingNote: UNHCR Global Focus publishes subsequent funding and expenditure updates.
appeals.delivery: UNHCR field operations with governments and partner organizations

appeals.name: WFP 2026 Operational Plan
appeals.latest: WFP’s 2026 planning assumptions allow assistance for approximately 110 million beneficiaries; its mid-year outlook reported life-saving support sustained for more than 45 million people.
appeals.brief: Funding constraints affect beneficiary counts, transfer duration and ration size, so planned and reached populations must remain distinct. The 110 million figure is an operational planning envelope, not a confirmed year-end reach.
appeals.fundingNote: The management plan states planned beneficiaries; current resource availability must be read from WFP funding reporting.
appeals.delivery: In-kind food, cash-based transfers and services through WFP country plans

appeals.name: Afghanistan HAC 2026
appeals.latest: UNICEF requested $949.1 million to reach 12 million people, including 6.5 million children, with life-saving aid and basic services.
appeals.brief: The appeal combines immediate humanitarian services with community resilience. The widest gap between need and planned reach is about 9.9 million people, based on the published need and target figures—not an estimate of exclusion by sector.
appeals.fundingNote: Funding coverage must be updated from UNICEF Afghanistan situation reports.
appeals.delivery: UNICEF and partners, including cross-border returnee response
milestones: Situation reports track reach and receipts

appeals.name: Sudan HAC 2026
appeals.latest: By mid-year UNICEF had mobilized $351 million against its $962.9 million appeal, leaving a reported 64% funding gap while reaching millions through health, nutrition, WASH and education services.
appeals.brief: Sudan is the only country record here with a dated, source-reported mid-year receipt total. Coverage is therefore calculated directly from displayed amounts; other appeals remain explicitly unscored until comparable reporting is available.
appeals.fundingNote: $351 million mobilized by 30 June 2026; UNICEF reports a 64% gap.
appeals.delivery: UNICEF and partners across all 18 states

appeals.name: State of Palestine HAC 2026
appeals.geography: Gaza Strip and West Bank, including East Jerusalem
appeals.latest: UNICEF sought $707.8 million for life-saving WASH, health, nutrition, education, protection, social protection and cash assistance across the Gaza Strip and West Bank.
appeals.brief: The programme publishes service-specific targets rather than one total beneficiary figure. Read each sector target independently because the same person may receive more than one service.
appeals.fundingNote: The public appeal page provides the requirement; current receipts are reported in situation reports.
appeals.delivery: UNICEF-supported facilities, systems and humanitarian partners

appeals.name: Somalia HAC 2026
appeals.latest: UNICEF requested $121 million to reach 1.2 million people, including 744,000 children, prioritizing nutrition, health, WASH and child protection.
appeals.brief: The response is deliberately concentrated on the most vulnerable quarter of the published population in need. Sector targets overlap, so they should not be summed as unique beneficiaries.
appeals.fundingNote: Current coverage is reported through UNICEF Somalia situation reports.
appeals.delivery: Integrated community services and local partnerships
milestones: UNICEF called for urgent support as malnutrition worsened

appeals.name: Yemen HAC 2026
appeals.latest: UNICEF requested $146.3 million to provide essential services to 5.2 million people, including 3.5 million children.
appeals.brief: The appeal is tightly prioritized relative to the 19.7 million people reported in need. Health, nutrition and emergency coordination are the stated funding priorities; target figures should not be read as full national coverage.
appeals.fundingNote: Current receipts should be checked against the latest UNICEF Yemen situation report.
appeals.delivery: Multisectoral services with government and local partners
milestones: Funding and programme outputs updated in situation reports

appeals.name: Haiti HAC 2026
appeals.latest: UNICEF requested $256.6 million to assist 1.7 million people in Haiti, including 1.2 million children.
appeals.brief: The programme focuses on conflict- and disaster-affected children and families. Funding and delivery should be monitored against the latest situation report because the appeal page is a planning baseline.
appeals.fundingNote: Current funding coverage is not stated in the appeal summary.
appeals.delivery: UNICEF and implementing partners in high-risk communities
milestones: Situation reports track funding and programme reach

appeals.name: Ukraine HAC 2026
appeals.latest: UNICEF appealed for $350 million to provide life-saving humanitarian assistance to 4.3 million people in Ukraine, including 725,000 children.
appeals.brief: The appeal combines emergency services and support to essential systems as the war continues. The published target is a programme planning figure and should be compared with subsequent service-level reach.
appeals.fundingNote: Current coverage should be verified in UNICEF Ukraine situation reports.
appeals.delivery: UNICEF-supported national and local systems and partners
milestones: Implementation aligned with Ukraine response planning

appeals.name: Burkina Faso HAC 2026
appeals.latest: UNICEF sought $168.9 million to deliver health, nutrition, WASH, education and child-protection interventions to 2.9 million people, including 2.5 million children.
appeals.brief: Children constitute most of the published target population. Operational review should focus on access, nutrition treatment continuity and safe service delivery in conflict-affected areas.
appeals.fundingNote: The appeal PDF states the requirement and target; subsequent receipts require situation-report verification.
appeals.delivery: UNICEF with government, local and international partners

appeals.name: Lebanon HAC 2026
appeals.latest: UNICEF revised its 2026 appeal to $388.5 million to reach 2 million people, including 700,000 children, after renewed conflict escalation.
appeals.brief: The revision expands beyond the original plan and includes displaced people, refugees, host communities and returnees. Monitor the revised requirement separately from funding received under the original appeal.
appeals.fundingNote: Current receipts should be reconciled against the revised appeal, not the original plan.
appeals.delivery: UNICEF systems support and partner delivery to displaced and host communities
